name: Delta II
best_known_for: NASA's medium-lift planetary-science workhorse — 155 flights 1989-2018, including Dawn, Messenger, MRO, Phoenix, Kepler, Spitzer, GRAIL, and the original GPS Block II constellation
credit: Two- or three-stage liquid-LOX/RP-1 first stage (Rocketdyne RS-27A) with up to nine GEM-40 / GEM-46 strap-on SRBs and a Star-48B solid-kick third stage for high-energy missions. 155 launches 1989-02-14 (Navstar II-1) through 2018-09-15 (ICESat-2), with a 99.4% success rate that made it NASA's go-to for planetary probes too heavy for Pegasus and too light to justify Atlas / Delta IV. The 7000-series evolved out of the post-Challenger GPS requirement; the 7920H + Star-48B 'Delta II Heavy' variant launched Dawn (2007) and Messenger (2004). Retired after the company merged its medium-lift line into Atlas V + Falcon 9.
